# Sharp products force abnormal hinge stress unless the simplex is regular

This is an exact qualification of the Fritz--John system in
`candidate de8d1a3251731edd`, Section 5.
It strengthens the statement that its objective multiplier might be
zero: for nonregular simplex products, it MUST be zero at the exact
sharp cap budget and minimal covering cap count.

Let n>=1,d>=2, let K be a d-simplex, and consider
S={0,1}^n x K. Set N=2^n(d+1). At the cap budget gamma_d |K|,
every feasible N-cap cover has the canonical local structure proved in
`candidate 0e807db2bba0c137`: exactly one
continuously normalized centroid vertex cap of each of the d+1 types
on each binary fiber, with zero cap volume on the other fibers.

If any joint Fritz--John system (15)--(18) for this cover has a positive
objective multiplier alpha_0, then K is regular. Conversely, when K
is regular, a system with alpha_0=1 and all budget multipliers zero
exists. Thus abnormality is intrinsic on nonregular sharp products;
it cannot be excluded by an unconditional constraint qualification.

## 1. Cover certificates and their actual contacts

Let g be the centroid of K. Fix a binary fiber p. Every cap belonging
to another fiber has STRICTLY negative margin at (p,g): if it contained
this interior point, its nonzero continuous normal would give positive
cap volume on p, contradicting its zero other-fiber mass.

The d+1 local canonical caps all have zero margin at g and their
intersection of complementary closed halfspaces is exactly {g}.
Consequently F_p=0. Any maximizing coverage certificate lambda_p has
all weights on these local caps: its weighted value at g is at most
zero, while its minimum is zero, so no strictly negative other-cap
margin may receive weight. It also has resultant U_p=0, because g is
an interior minimizer of the affine function U_p dot x. The local
simplex facet normals have a unique dependence up to scaling, with
all coefficients positive. Thus every local cap has positive weight.

The actual primal-dual contact selected in the joint system is g:
all the local canonical inequalities L_i<=0 together force every
barycentric coordinate to be at most 1/(d+1), hence equal to it.

## 2. Integer extremality removes other-fiber section forces

Take one cap i whose local fiber is p. Write its cap mass as c_i>0,
so P_i=c_i p. The right sides of (15)--(16) involve only p, by the
certificate support just proved. Subtract p times (15) from (16):

    r_i(P_i^s-pS_i)=0.                                (1)

The effective section masses t_z>=0 satisfy
P_i^s-pS_i=sum_z t_z(z-p). The globally affine binary distance

    q_p(z)=sum_k[(1-p_k)z_k+p_k(1-z_k)]

vanishes at p and is strictly positive at every other binary vertex.
Applying its linear part to (1) gives

    r_i sum_z t_z q_p(z)=0.

Thus r_i t_z=0 for every z!=p. Supporting sections on other fibers,
including facet coincidences, cannot contribute to the multiplied
section moment in this equation.

The own-fiber section is proper, so its effective trace density is
one. Its centroid is exactly g: a section parallel to the opposite
facet at barycentric level 1/(d+1) has that same value for every
coordinate of its section centroid. Consequently

    r_i m_i^s=r_i S_i g.                              (2)

This also holds trivially when r_i=0. It uses no assumption that the
other supporting sections are absent geometrically.

## 3. A positive objective multiplier forces a regular simplex

Let v_j be the local cap's vertex, H_j its altitude, and u_i its unit
continuous normal pointing toward v_j. The canonical cap centroid
and hinge-to-volume ratio are

    g_i=g+(v_j-g)/(d+1),
    Psi_i/c_i=d H_j/(d+1)^2.                          (3)

Using the contact g, (2), and the mass equation (15), the joint
continuous-moment equation (17) reduces exactly to

    alpha_0 c_i(g_i-g)=alpha_0 Psi_i u_i.              (4)

If alpha_0>0, equations (3)--(4) imply

    v_j-g=[d H_j/(d+1)]u_i.                           (5)

Every vector from the centroid to a vertex is therefore perpendicular
to that vertex's opposite facet.

For completeness, this forces regularity in every d>=2. Put
w_j=v_j-g, so sum_j w_j=0. Orthogonality says w_i dot w_j is independent
of j!=i. Symmetry of the inner product shows these off-diagonal values
are the same constant c for all i,j, i!=j. Taking the inner product
with sum_j w_j=0 gives |w_i|^2=-d c for every i. Hence every squared
edge length equals

    |w_i-w_j|^2=-2(d+1)c.

The vertices are distinct, so this common length is positive. All
edges are equal and the simplex is regular, as asserted.

If the simplex is regular, all altitudes are equal and all local
certificate weights are 1/(d+1). Set alpha_0=1, r_i=0 and, on each
fiber, eta_p=(d+1)gamma_d |K|. The mass and integer equations hold
immediately. Regularity makes (5), hence the continuous moment
equation, hold as well. The lambda equations hold because the local
cap values at g are zero and all other values are negative; the
required active simplex multipliers are their nonnegative deficits.
Set the sphere multipliers to -Psi_i. This supplies the claimed normal
system and proves the converse.

This result does not contradict the positive attained hinge potential:
it concerns the multipliers of a constrained first-order system. Nor
does it show that a different body-volume variational problem has
abnormal multipliers. Its conclusion is confined to the fixed-measure,
exact-budget full-cover hinge problem just specified.
